messages:
alex: New hire onboarding blocked. They used `pipx` to try the quickstart and hit an import error when importing the async client. Seems to be a dependency/resolution difference compared to following the poetry quickstart. Logs below.

alex: ```
$ pipx install redwood-python-sdk
Installing collected packages: typing-extensions, ...
ERROR: Cannot import name 'TypeAlias' from 'typing_extensions'
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/private/var/.../site-packages/redwood/client/async_client.py\", line 12, in <module>
    from typing_extensions import TypeAlias
ImportError: cannot import name 'TypeAlias' from 'typing_extensions'
```

alex: Environment: macOS M1, Python 3.10.6, pip 23.2, pipx 1.2.0. When the same user followed the poetry instructions (`poetry install`) it worked locally.

jamie: pipx creates a separate venv and uses pip to resolve and install packages; it won't use poetry.lock unless you export a requirements.txt. If our published wheel is missing mac arm assets or our PyPI release only has sdist, pip will build from source and pull transitive deps differently.

kevin: Two likely causes: 1) pipx/pip resolution pulled an older `typing-extensions` (no TypeAlias); 2) we published no mac arm wheels so pip falls back to build path that requires Rust / builds cryptography and sometimes picks different transitive versions.

jamie: Quick triage commands: `pipx runpip redwood-python-sdk freeze` inside pipx venv and compare to `poetry lock --no-update` resolved versions. Also try `pip install --prefer-binary redwood-python-sdk` to prefer prebuilt wheels.

alex: I did those. `pipx runpip freeze` showed `typing-extensions==4.0.1`. Our `poetry.lock` currently resolves `typing-extensions = \"^4.6\"` but our PyPI release artifacts (release 0.10.0) only uploaded manylinux and x86 mac wheels, no arm. So pip on M1 fell back to source and resolved older transitive constraint to 4.0.1.

kevin: Actionable fixes: A) Pin `typing-extensions = \">=4.6.0,<5\"` in pyproject.toml so any pip resolver picks a compatible version even when transitive deps are loose. B) Publish macosx_11_0_universal2 wheels via cibuildwheel so pipx installs binaries on M1. C) Add a short postinstall import check in our quickstart script that fails fast with a clear message.

docswriter: For onboarding docs: add a troubleshooting note under \"Install\" that explains `pipx` vs `poetry` differences and recommends `pip install --prefer-binary` or `poetry install` in a venv. Example snippet to add: 
```
If you used `pipx` and see native build or typing errors, try:
1. python -m pip install --upgrade pip wheel setuptools
2. pip install --prefer-binary redwood-python-sdk
3. or use `poetry install` in the project directory
```
Also add a short sentence: \"If you maintain a locked requirements.txt for CI/pipx use, ensure `typing-extensions >= 4.6` is present.\"

jamie: I also suggest adding an automated smoke test in CI that simulates pipx/pip install behavior: create a clean venv on macos-13 runner, run `pip install redwood-python-sdk==${{ release }}` (without build isolation if needed), then run `python -c \"import redwood.client.async_client\"`. That will surface both wheel availability and typing incompat issues.

ci-bot: FYI: release 0.10.0 artifacts show missing mac arm wheels (only manylinux_x86_64 and macosx_x86_64). See CI release logs https://ci.redwood.example/7890.

kevin: I'll queue a small release pipeline change to build mac universal wheels and re-upload. Also opening a quick PR to pin `typing-extensions` and add the mac install smoke test in the release matrix. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/1833 (WIP).

docswriter: I'll update CONTRIBUTING and the quickstart to include the `--prefer-binary` tip plus a one-liner about `pipx` isolation. Also adding a brief note for maintainers: \"When exporting requirements for pipx or CI, prefer `poetry export --format requirements.txt --without-hashes` and ensure typing-extensions pins are included.\"

alex: One extra idea: include a tiny `scripts/quickstart-install.sh` in the repo used by the onboarding guide that does `python -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate && poetry install` so new hires get a deterministic path. That avoids pipx surprises.

kevin: Good. We'll prioritize: 1) pin typing-extensions; 2) publish mac universal wheels; 3) add macos editable/pipx smoke tests; 4) docs + quickstart script. If we need a fast hotfix we can add a short try/except import fallback in async_client.py, but prefer dependency + wheel fixes so we don't mask other issues.

alex: Thanks all 44d. I'll file the onboarding bug, link PRs, and add a short note to the new-hire checklist until the wheels are published.
